multipleChoice.question: What main issue is raised by the boy’s informal greeting?
options: Whether famous people should accept slang in public conversations.
Whether politeness depends on interpretation as well as wording.
Whether children should be banned from using informal language.
Whether greetings are polite only when they include a person’s name.

multipleChoice.question: Why did the boy use the word “thingy”?
options: He wanted to insult the person by refusing to say his name.
He was quoting a phrase commonly used by young children.
He was unsure whether the person was actually famous.
He recognised the person but could not remember his name.

multipleChoice.question: How did the person addressed interpret the boy’s greeting?
options: He saw it as friendly rather than threatening or insulting.
He considered it aggressive because of the missing name.
He thought it was formally correct but emotionally cold.
He felt it proved young people no longer learn manners.

multipleChoice.question: Why can the boy’s words be judged differently by different listeners?
options: The phrase “innit” has no meaning outside formal English.
A formal greeting would have made the words less clear.
Politeness depends partly on how the listener perceives them.
Adults and children follow exactly the same social rules.

multipleChoice.question: What contrast is made between the boy’s language and its effect?
options: It was highly informal, yet it was not experienced as offensive.
It was grammatically polished, yet it sounded socially distant.
It used a person’s full name, yet it still created confusion.
It was intended as an insult, yet it produced no reaction.

multipleChoice.question: What opinion about teaching politeness is presented?
options: Children should learn politeness only after they become adults.
Politeness is mainly useful for avoiding punishment at school.
Social rules matter less than a child’s private intentions.
Politeness helps children gain acceptance within society.

multipleChoice.question: In the expert’s explanation, what does the “crucial thing” refer to?
options: The exact slang word chosen by the boy.
The way the listener understood the remark.
The social status of the person in the street.
The choice between formal and informal grammar.

multipleChoice.question: What can be inferred from the nursery-school incident?
options: The cook was angry because the child spoke too informally.
The parent believed greetings were unnecessary at that age.
The child’s silence felt like a failure to meet social expectations.
The other children were embarrassed by the parent’s reaction.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the nursery-school story included?
options: To show how social pressure around children’s manners is felt in practice.
To prove that very young children are naturally offensive to adults.
To argue that polite behaviour matters only inside schools.
To explain why adults should ignore children’s bad behaviour.

multipleChoice.question: What overall implication does the discussion suggest?
options: Politeness is fixed, so intention and context should be ignored.
Informal speech is normally more polite than formal language.
Teaching politeness is pointless because offence is subjective.
Politeness is subjective but still has real social value.
